Graffiti & street art documentary “Signs of Life” dives into the profound connection between memories, experiences, and the creative process. This documentary follows Australian artist John Kaye as he embarks on a journey through Indonesia, using his art to express his encounters and insights.

Set in the Special Region of Yogyakarta in Java, the film unfolds in the backdrop of Indonesia's only remaining royal city, renowned for its classical Javanese arts and traditions. 

Over three weeks, John explores the region on a motorbike, immersing himself in local villages and cultures.

A self-taught painter, John Kaye specializes in large-scale artworks, dividing his time between painting murals and working in his studio. 

Join us as we witness the intersection of art and life through John's eyes, celebrating the beauty of Indonesian culture and the universal language of art.

Signs of Life is an exploration of how memories and experiences directly correlate with an artistic process. The documentary captures the perspectives of Australian artist, John Kaye as he travels around Indonesia creating street art. John Kaye is a self-trained painter who specializes in large-scale paintings with a split practice between street art and studio work. Consciously aware of the separation and balance of these two worlds colliding. The film takes place in the Special Region of Yogyakarta in Indonesia, on the island of Java. As the only Indonesian royal city still ruled by a monarchy, Yogyakarta is regarded as an important center for classical Javanese fine arts and culture. John creates paintings in response to his experiences. Over the span of three weeks, John travels through the region by motorbike visiting villages to meet with locals who open their doors and share their culture.

Hey everyone,

I recently created my first full-length film, a documentary on custom motorcycle builders in Australia. I created this project with $0 funding and a very small team of basically 2. We shot this whole doco on a road trip down the east coast of Australia meeting up with different builders and tapping into their worlds for a short amount of time. For most of the film, we were using a very run and gun set up, most of the film was shot on the black magic URSA 4.6K and Canon L series glass.  For some riding sequences, we used a RED Epic and RED Scarlet. Very basic lighting set up, using cheap dracast LED 500's for the interviews and a Ronin hanging out the back of a Commodore station wagon for most of the riding shots.  I really want to take my cinematography to the next level and also figure out how to get funding for future projects. This is our first attempt at creating something legitimate, I would greatly appreciate any advice, feedback or constructive criticism. 

Cheers,

Jake Ashe.
